notes:
Replication title and authors verified against assigned reference using the primary OSF preprint. Values are from the final sample, not supplementary full-sample analysis. Authors support the directional hypothesis while describing the effect magnitudes as inconsistent with and larger than the original. Original statistics quoted or recalculated by the replication authors were not substituted for unavailable original primary text. Acquisition attempts: original DOI landing page 403; OpenAlex showed no best_oa_location and supplied a historical Stanford author PDF; CiteSeer PDF 404 via terminal and inaccessible via web; historical Stanford author PDF connection failed. No paid or signed-in acquisition.
Source follow-up: Published 1999 Cognitive Psychology article, Goals as Reference Points, by Chip Heath, Richard P. Larrick and George Wu. Unassigned replication is a placeholder. n lists the two printed condition sample sizes (65 do-your-best; 66 specific goal), without deriving a combined N. The printed p value is for their comparison, not a separate within-condition test. No numerical chi-square statistic is printed.
